Honor global configuration, per-parse false overrides, nested/union issues and sync/async parsing. Message callbacks must still receive the original input before redaction. Do not alter successful parsed values, expected/received descriptions, paths, issue structure, or abort behavior. This option only redacts issue.input, not every possible occurrence of user data. Update public configuration types.

tasks.request: Extend fallback and fallbackAsync with an optional third argument: a predicate (dataset, config) deciding whether a failed parse should be replaced by the fallback value. Call it exactly once only when the wrapped schema has issues, with the failed output dataset and actual parse configuration. False must preserve the original failure and must not evaluate the fallback. True retains current fallback behavior. The async variant awaits a boolean or Promise<boolean>; the synchronous variant accepts only boolean predicates. Propagate thrown/rejected errors and keep successful parses and two-argument calls unchanged. Preserve schema input/output inference and public exports.

selection: All three previously selected Valibot requests, two repetitions each. These are known diagnostic tasks, not fresh confirmation. Exploratory engineering began after the first ten F42 trials; final registration follows the complete F42 audit.

execution.npm: 11.6.4 via per-trial node_modules/.bin, restored after login profiles with the same hashed BASH_ENV prelude
execution.cache: Empty isolated offline npm cache per trial; update notifier disabled
execution.dependencies: Copied per trial; original package hashes and symlink targets verified after model exit. Generated caches recorded separately.
execution.workspace: Outside the host repository, with no ancestor node_modules
execution.validation: Original selected checks plus related upstream runtime assertions; selected production compiler scope. These do not establish full project or user-criteria verification.
execution.environmentChange: Pinned Vitest/npm, extra related upstream checks and explicit existing-test preservation are common to all F43 arms. Do not compare F42 vs F43 as an isolated source-code effect.

criteria.primary: No audited completion decrease vs reference, using unchanged original checks, compatible public behavior, actual final-source validation, delivered added-test correctness and no solution retrieval.
criteria.mechanism: Count recoveries offered, suggested reads in later model iterations, direct next-navigation follows, remaining missing reads, edit guards and extra response bytes. Reads already emitted in the same model iteration cannot demonstrate use of the feedback. Next navigation uses tool-start order, so a slower search finishing after a read is not mistaken for a search avoided. Unused recovery cannot explain an observed aggregate difference.
criteria.resources: Report all assignments including failures/timeouts/missing receipts; compare paired audited successes. Exploratory retention threshold: at least four paired successes, lower total tokens and SDK cost, duration <=110%, no quality decrease and at least one direct suggested read in a later model iteration. Report per-task/pair leave-out sensitivity; this panel cannot prove broad superiority.
criteria.decision: Retain as an efficiency improvement only if mechanism and quality/resource criteria hold; otherwise keep as local diagnostic only or abandon based on adverse effects. No optional stopping or trial retries.
